arxiv-2007-00410.title: A time adaptive multirate Dirichlet–Neumann waveform relaxation method for heterogeneous coupled heat equations
arxiv-2007-00410.creator: Peter Meisrimel, Azahar Monge, Philipp Birken
arxiv-2007-00410.description: Abstract We consider partitioned time integration for heterogeneous coupled heat equations. First and second order multirate, as well as time-adaptive Dirichlet-Neumann Waveform relaxation (DNWR) methods are derived. In 1D and for implicit Euler time integration, we analytically determine optimal relaxation parameters for the fully discrete scheme.

arxiv-2012-14358.title: Attractor invariants, brane tilings and crystals
arxiv-2012-14358.creator: Sergey Mozgovoy, Boris Pioline
arxiv-2012-14358.description: Abstract . Supersymmetric D-brane bound states on a Calabi-Yau threefold 𝒳 \mathcal{X} are counted by generalized Donaldsdon-Thomas invariants Ω 𝖹 ​ ( γ ) \Omega_{\mathsf{Z}}(\gamma) , depending on a Chern character (or electromagnetic charge) γ ∈ H ∗ ​ ( 𝒳 ) \gamma\in H^{*}(\mathcal{X}) and a stability condition (or central charge) 𝖹 \mathsf{Z} .

arxiv-2103-06934.title: Singularity analysis and analytic solutions for the Benney-Gjevik equations
arxiv-2103-06934.creator: Andronikos Paliathanasis, Genly Leon, P.G.L. Leach
arxiv-2103-06934.description: Abstract We apply the Painlevé Test for the Benney and the Benney-Gjevik equations which describe waves in falling liquids. We prove that these two nonlinear 1 + 1 1+1 evolution equations pass the singularity test for the travelling-wave solutions. The algebraic solutions in terms of Laurent expansions are presented.

arxiv-2112-01973.title: Yang–Mills–Scalar–Matter Fields in the Quantum Hopf Fibration
arxiv-2112-01973.creator: Gustavo Amilcar Saldaña Moncada
arxiv-2112-01973.description: Abstract . In this paper we present solutions to the non–commutative geometrical version of the Yang–Mills–Scalar–Matter theory in the Hopf fibration S 1 ↪ S 3 → S 2 S^{1}\hookrightarrow S^{3}\rightarrow S^{2} using the 3 ​ D 3D –calculus. MSC 2010: 46L87, 58B99. Keywords: Fields, quantum Hopf fibration, canonical quantum principal connection 1.

arxiv-2112-09331.title: Contrastive Vision-Language Pre-training with Limited Resources
arxiv-2112-09331.creator: Quan Cui, Boyan Zhou, Yu Guo, Weidong Yin, Hao Wu, Osamu Yoshie, Yubo Chen
arxiv-2112-09331.description: Abstract Pioneering dual-encoder pre-training works ( e.g. , CLIP and ALIGN) have revealed the potential of aligning multi-modal representations with contrastive learning. However, these works require a tremendous amount of data and computational resources ( e.g. , billion-level web data and hundreds of GPUs), which prevent researchers with limited resources from reproduction and further exploration.

arxiv-2211-17080.title: Trust and Time Preference: Measuring a Causal Effect in a Random-Assignment Experiment
arxiv-2211-17080.creator: Linas Nasvytis
arxiv-2211-17080.description: Abstract Large amounts of evidence suggest that trust levels in a country are an important determinant of its macroeconomic growth. In this paper, we investigate one channel through which trust might support economic performance: through the levels of patience, also known as time preference in the economics literature.

arxiv-2303-16528.title: Building a Knowledge Graph of Distributed Ledger Technologies Volume: 0
arxiv-2303-16528.creator: L.Lukas Königlabel=e1]lukas.koenig@fhstp.ac.at, S.Sebastian Neumaierlabel=e2]sebastian.neumaier@fhstp.ac.at
arxiv-2303-16528.description: Abstract Distributed ledger systems have become more prominent and successful in recent years, with a focus on blockchains and cryptocurrency. This has led to various misunderstandings about both the technology itself and its capabilities, as in many cases blockchain and cryptocurrency is used synonymously and other applications are often overlooked.

arxiv-2307-05111.title: Density fluctuations for the multi-species stirring process
arxiv-2307-05111.creator: Francesco Casini, Cristian Giardinà, Frank Redig
arxiv-2307-05111.description: Abstract We study the density fluctuations at equilibrium of the multi-species stirring process, a natural multi-type generalization of the symmetric (partial) exclusion process. In the diffusive scaling limit, the resulting process is a system of infinite-dimensional Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes that are coupled in the noise terms.

arxiv-2307-15851.title: High-Energy Neutrino and Gamma Ray Production in Clusters of Galaxies
arxiv-2307-15851.creator: Elisabete M. de Gouveia Dal Pino
arxiv-2307-15851.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Elisabete M. de Gouveia Dal Pino. We compute the contribution from clusters of galaxies to the diffuse neutrino and γ − \gamma- ray background. Due to their unique magnetic-field configuration, cosmic rays (CRs) with energy ≤ 10 17 \leq 10^{17} eV can be confined within these structures over cosmological time scales, and generate secondary particles, including neutrinos and gamma-rays, through interactions with the background gas and photons.

arxiv-2311-00104.title: Multi-functional OFDM Signal Design for Integrated Sensing, Communications, and Power Transfer
arxiv-2311-00104.creator: Yumeng Zhang, Sundar Aditya, Bruno Clerckx
arxiv-2311-00104.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yumeng Zhang, Sundar Aditya, Bruno Clerckx. The wireless domain is witnessing a flourishing of integrated systems, e.g. (a) integrated sensing and communications, and (b) simultaneous wireless information and power transfer, due to their potential to use resources (spectrum, power) judiciously. Inspired by this trend, we investigate integrated sensing, communications and powering (ISCAP), through the design of a wideband OFDM signal to power a sensor while simultaneously performing target-sensing and communication.

arxiv-2412-07013.title: Charge asymmetry in the Heisenberg model
arxiv-2412-07013.creator: Rohit Hegde
arxiv-2412-07013.description: Abstract Supplementing the Heisenberg model with a Hubbard-commuting kinetic of electrons adds to its spectrum without interference. One consequence is the precise incorporation of canonical linear spin wave theory within the time-dependent Hartree-Fock framework, as pure localization emerges from itinerant dynamics. This embedding method generalizes to all spin-½ models and is expected to extend to multi-orbital systems.

arxiv-2505-22905.title: Profiling and optimization of multi-card GPU machine learning jobs
arxiv-2505-22905.creator: Marcin Lawenda, Kyrylo Khloponin, Krzesimir Samborski, Łukasz Szustak
arxiv-2505-22905.description: Abstract The effectiveness and efficiency of machine learning methodologies are crucial, especially with respect to the quality of results and computational cost. This paper discusses different model optimization techniques, providing a comprehensive analysis of key performance indicators. Several parallelization strategies for image recognition, adapted to different hardware and software configurations, including distributed data parallelism and distributed hardware processing, are analyzed.

pmc-10589804.title: Pharmacy Benefit Manager Pricing and Spread Pricing for High-Utilization Generic Drugs
pmc-10589804.creator: T. Joseph Mattingly, Kenechukwu C. Ben-Umeh, Ge Bai, Gerard F. Anderson
pmc-10589804.description: This cross-sectional study uses Medicare Part D claims for high-utilization generic drugs to analyze gross profits accumulated by pharmacy benefit managers, pharmacies, wholesalers, and manufacturers in the pharmaceutical supply chain. Introduction The practice by pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) of spread pricing—charging the client (ie, insurer) a higher amount than is reimbursed to the pharmacy—has garnered substantial attention from policymakers.

pmc-10737335.title: UNIQUE MICROBIOME SIGNATURES RELATED TO CANCER SURVIVORSHIP AND COGNITIVE DECLINE IN OLDER ADULTS
pmc-10737335.creator: Jayden Haggler, Brandi Miller, Diptaraj Chaudhari, Hariom Yadav, Shalini Jain
pmc-10737335.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Significant scientific advancements have resulted in new and effective therapies for patients with cancer. Although this leads to an increased cancer survivor population, there are several long-term side effects of cancer treatments, including a high risk of developing dementia. Emerging evidence shows that the gut microbiota significantly contributes to brain health and dementia pathology; however, its role in cancer treatment-related side effects, specifically in older adults, is not well known.

pmc-11345371.title: Optical coherence tomography angiography findings in patients affected by giant cell arteritis, with and without ocular involvement: a pilot study
pmc-11345371.creator: Lorenzo Vannozzi, Cristina Nicolosi, Giulio Vicini, Daniela Bacherini, Dario Giattini, Maria Letizia Urban, Adalgisa Palermo, Danilo Malandrino, Federica Bello, Gianni Virgili, Fabrizio Giansanti
pmc-11345371.description: PurposeWe evaluated the clinical features and retinal and disk perfusion characteristics by using optical coherence tomography (OCT) and optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) in a subset of giant cell arteritis (GCA) patients who manifested anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (AION), in a subset of GCA patients without ocular involvement, and in a control group composed of healthy controls.

pmc-11625738.title: Shedding light on negative cultures in osteoarticular infections: leveraging mNGS to unravel risk factors and microbial profiles
pmc-11625738.creator: Haiqi Ding, Jiexin Huang, Lan Lin, Yang Chen, Qijin Wang, Wenbo Li, Ying Huang, Xinyu Fang, Wenming Zhang
pmc-11625738.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundThe objective of this study is to utilize metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) to analyze the risk factors causing negative microbial cultures, comprehensively delineate the microbial profiles neglected by traditional cultures, and optimize the pathogenetic diagnostic procedure accordingly.Research design and methodsWe enrolled 341 patients diagnosed with OI at our center between 2016 and 2022, and gathered data including age, gender, clinical diagnosis, duration of antibiotic use prior to sampling, microbial culture results, and mNGS results for these patients.

pmc-12593588.title: Structure-guided in silico design of a methionine aminopeptidase–derived multi-epitope vaccine candidate against Neisseria gonorrhoeae
pmc-12593588.creator: Sinethemba H. Yakobi, Uchechukwu U. Nwodo
pmc-12593588.description: Escalating antimicrobial resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae underscores the need for vaccine strategies that avoid the pathogen's highly variable outer-membrane antigens.This study pursued an epitope-focused approach targeting methionine aminopeptidase (MAP), an essential, evolutionarily constrained metalloenzyme. An AlphaFold2 model with high confidence (mean pLDDT 90) guided mapping of solvent-exposed, non-catalytic loops, excluding residues within 15 Å of the catalytic H82/D110/H173/D206/E237 cluster.

pmc-13280430.title: The effects of mindfulness meditation on burnout in clinical genetic counselors: A three‐arm randomized controlled trial
pmc-13280430.creator: Colleen Caleshu, MaryAnn Campion, Jehannine (J9) Austin, Philippe Goldin, Julia Silver, Aad Tibben
pmc-13280430.description: Burnout is common among genetic counselors (GCs). Clinician burnout has been found to adversely affect individual well‐being, patient care, and the likelihood of staying in a role. Both individual and system‐level solutions are needed to address burnout. Mindfulness meditation (MM) is one individual‐level solution that has shown promise for reducing burnout in clinicians, but has not been studied in GCs.

pmc-13315178.title: Role-specific patterns of work-related musculoskeletal disorders across nursing settings: a comparative study of operating room, intensive care unit, and ward nurses
pmc-13315178.creator: Dichao Zheng, Hui Yu
pmc-13315178.description: BackgroundNurses are at high risk for work-related musculoskeletal disorders. While previous studies often focus on single populations, comparative data across different specialties, including Operating Room, Intensive Care Unit, and General Ward, are limited. This study aimed to compare the prevalence patterns of work-related musculoskeletal disorders across these three distinct nursing roles.

pmc-13407608.title: Komplikationen der akuten Otitis media
pmc-13407608.creator: Lukas Schmutzler, Matthias Santer, Daniel Dejaco, Benedikt Hofauer, Joachim Schmutzhard
pmc-13407608.description: Komplikationen der akuten Otitis media (AOM) sind selten, können jedoch intratemporal oder intrakraniell auftreten. Klinisch relevante Mastoiditiden zeigen sich meist durch subperiostale Abszesse, während subklinische Verschattungen der Mastoidzellen häufig auftreten, aber keine spezifische Therapie erfordern. Weitere mögliche Komplikationen umfassen Labyrinthitis, Fazialisparese, intratemporale Abszesse, Sinusvenenthrombosen oder Meningitiden. Die Diagnostik basiert auf klinischer Untersuchung, Laborparametern und gezielter Bildgebung.

pmc-13536027.title: Patient Self‐Reported Global Satisfaction With Rivaroxaban in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation: A Comparison Between Oral Anticoagulation‐Naïve Versus Oral Anticoagulation‐Experienced Patients
pmc-13536027.creator: Bogdan G. Markovic, Miroslav Mihajlovic, Aleksandar Kocijancic, Jelena Simic, Milan Marinkovic, Vladan Kovacevic, Milica Ivanisevic, Nikola Isailovic, Nebojsa Mujovic, Belma Pojskic, Tatjana Potpara, the GUARDIAN Investigators
pmc-13536027.description: BackgroundLong‐term oral anticoagulant therapy (OAC) is essential to effective stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF), but adherence to OAC is a concern. Patient self‐reported satisfaction with OAC is a major contributor to OAC adherence. We compared the levels of and time trends in patient global satisfaction with rivaroxaban in OAC‐naïve and OAC‐experienced AF patients.

uslaw-usc-t25-s1911.description: United States Code, Title 25 (Indians); Chapter 21 (Indian Child Welfare); Subchapter I (Child Custody Proceedings). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Exclusive jurisdiction An Indian tribe shall have jurisdiction exclusive as to any State over any child custody proceeding involving an Indian child who resides or is domiciled within the reservation of such tribe, except where such jurisdiction is otherwise vested.
